description: Carbon is a versatile non-metal that forms millions of compounds due to its unique properties of catenation and tetravalency. This study guide covers the fundamental properties of carbon, hydrocarbons, functional groups, and key organic chemical reactions.

sections.title: Basic Properties of Carbon
sections.description: Introduction to the valency of carbon and its unique bonding nature.

key_concepts.explanation: A chemical bond formed by the sharing of electron pairs between atoms. Carbon always forms covalent bonds to achieve a stable noble gas configuration.
The unique property of carbon atoms to form bonds with other carbon atoms, resulting in long straight chains, branched chains, or ring structures.
Carbon has 4 electrons in its outermost valence shell. It bonds with four other atoms to complete its octet and achieve stability.

important_facts.fact: The atomic number of Carbon is 6, and its electronic configuration is 2, 4.

sections.title: Allotropes of Carbon
sections.description: Different physical forms of the same element that exhibit identical chemical properties but different physical properties.

key_concepts.explanation: The existence of an element in more than one physical form, varying in structural arrangement of atoms.

key_associations.extra_info: Each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid 3D structure. It is a poor conductor of electricity (insulator).
Carbon atoms are arranged in hexagonal arrays in layers. Used as a dry lubricant and in pencil leads.
Buckminsterfullerene consists of 60 carbon atoms (C-60) arranged in the shape of a geodesic dome.

sections.title: Hydrocarbons
sections.description: Classification of compounds made up entirely of carbon and hydrogen atoms.

key_concepts.explanation: Hydrocarbons in which all carbon atoms are linked by single covalent bonds. They are relatively unreactive and burn with a clean flame.
Hydrocarbons containing at least one double bond (Alkenes) or triple bond (Alkynes) between carbon atoms. They are highly reactive.

scientific_principles.application: Examples include Methane (CH4) and Ethane (C2H6), which are the main components of Biogas and CNG.
Example includes Ethene (C2H4), widely used in the ripening of fruits and the manufacturing of plastics like polythene.
Example includes Ethyne (C2H2), also known as Acetylene, which is used in oxy-acetylene torches for welding metals.

sections.title: Functional Groups and Homologous Series
sections.description: Specific groups of atoms that determine the chemical properties of organic compounds.

key_concepts.explanation: An atom or a group of atoms attached to a carbon chain that defines the specific chemical properties and reactivity of the compound.
A series of organic compounds having the same functional group and similar chemical properties, where successive members differ by a -CH2 unit.

key_associations.extra_info: Examples: Methanol, Ethanol. The IUPAC name ends with the suffix '-ol'.
Example: Methanal (Formaldehyde). The IUPAC name ends with the suffix '-al'. It is always located at the end of the chain.
Example: Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid). The IUPAC name ends with the suffix '-oic acid'.
Example: Propanone (Acetone). It is always located within the carbon chain, never at the ends. Suffix is '-one'.

sections.title: Important Organic Compounds and Chemical Reactions
sections.description: Crucial carbon compounds used in daily life and their industrial reaction pathways.

key_concepts.explanation: The active ingredient in all alcoholic drinks. It is an excellent solvent, used in medicines like tincture iodine, cough syrups, and tonics.
Commonly known as Acetic acid. A 3-4% aqueous solution of ethanoic acid is called vinegar, widely used as a preservative in pickles.

scientific_principles.application: Formation of an ester in the presence of an acid catalyst. Esters are sweet-smelling substances used extensively in making perfumes and flavoring agents.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: CH3COOC2H5 (Ester) + NaOH (Base) → C2H5OH (Alcohol) + CH3COONa (Sodium salt of carboxylic acid)
scientific_principles.application: The reaction of an ester with a strong base (like NaOH) to yield back the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid. This specific reaction is used in the preparation of soap.

important_facts.fact: The melting point of pure ethanoic acid is 290 K (17°C). Because it often freezes during winter in cold climates, it is historically called 'Glacial Acetic Acid'.
